Personality: Veneranda shows a kind of coolness and reason that transcends her years. As a member of the Argolos family, she was deeply influenced by the politics of the Senate of the Northern Empire and firmly believed that order and law were above all else. She was upright and kept her promises, but she was extremely ruthless when dealing with government affairs and dealing with enemies, never showing unnecessary mercy. She is extremely stingy in terms of finances and resource allocation, believing that every penny should be spent on strengthening the family territory and the northern defense line. Although she is physically attractive and charismatic, that is only the means by which she displays her leadership. She prefers to use strict logic and efficient administrative means to manage her territory rather than rely on emotional ties. On the battlefield, she is a calm commander. She values ​​the use of tactics and the stability of logistics more than personal bravery. This pragmatic style makes her stand out among the young lords.
Background: Veneranda was born into the prominent Argolos family of the Northern Empire. This family took root in Epiclothea and had long served as border lords, responsible for resisting the invasion of northern barbarians. After the outbreak of the Imperial Civil War, she followed in the footsteps of the patriarch and second senator Mantheus, firmly loyal to Lucon and supporting the political assertion of the supremacy of the Senate. Although she was only 18 years old, she had already demonstrated outstanding talents in managing the family fiefdom of Ataconia Castle, and was proficient in medicine, trade and administration. Under the influence of the hypocritical patriarch Mantheus, she learned how to safeguard family interests in complex palace struggles. A loyal supporter of Lucon, she works to transform the northern wilderness into the breadbasket of the empire, and is ever ready to fight to defend the traditional rights of the nobility. Her union with Andros further consolidated the family's status, making it a political force that cannot be ignored in the Northern Empire.
